elements.element: Vendor presently assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in deliverables created for Customer, so Customer owns them.
elements.evidence: The clause grants the Company a licence to deliverables but contains no assignment of deliverables or statement that the Company owns them.

elements.element: Vendor presently assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in work product created for Customer, so Customer owns it.
elements.evidence: There is no assignment or Customer-ownership provision covering work product; the licence covers only the Site and other deliverables.

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of all of its pre-existing IP.
elements.evidence: HDI retains ownership only of its generic tools and know-how. The clause does not cover all categories of pre-existing Vendor IP.

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to all Vendor IP embedded in the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The licence to use, modify and sublicense the Site and any other deliverables applies to the deliverables as a whole without excluding HDI tools or other Vendor IP embedded in them.

elements.element: The licence to Vendor IP embedded in the deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The deliverables licence is expressly perpetual.

elements.element: The licence to Vendor IP embedded in the deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The deliverables licence is expressly irrevocable.

elements.element: The licence to Vendor IP embedded in the deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The deliverables licence is expressly royalty-free.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The clause limits HDI's licence in certain Content and data but does not affirm that the Company retains all rights in all Customer Data.

elements.element: The intellectual-property allocation creates no joint ownership.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no express prohibition on joint ownership, and its ownership allocation is incomplete for deliverables and other work product.

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of its generic tools.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that HDI retains ownership of its generic tools.

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of its know-how.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that HDI retains ownership of its know-how.

elements.element: Customer receives a licence covering the deliverables developed for Customer.
elements.evidence: HDI expressly grants the Company a licence to the Site and any other deliverables developed for the Company under the Agreement.

elements.element: The deliverables licence is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The licence is expressly perpetual.

elements.element: The deliverables licence is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The licence is expressly irrevocable.

elements.element: The deliverables licence is worldwide.
elements.evidence: The licence is expressly worldwide.

elements.element: The deliverables licence is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The licence is expressly royalty-free.

elements.element: The deliverables licence permits Customer to use the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The licence expressly permits the Company to use the Site and other deliverables.

elements.element: The deliverables licence permits Customer to modify the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The licence expressly permits the Company to modify the Site and other deliverables.

elements.element: The deliverables licence permits Customer to sublicense the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The licence expressly permits the Company to sublicense the Site and other deliverables.

elements.element: Customer may exercise the deliverables licence for its business.
elements.evidence: The granted rights may expressly be exercised by the Company for its business.

result.reason: The operative redline fully implements the fallback ownership and licence package, but not the preferred assignment-based ownership, comprehensive pre-existing-IP reservation, Customer Data rights, or no-joint-ownership requirements. It is not minimal because it also adds an HDI Content/data-use restriction that is unnecessary to achieve the complete fallback. The addition does not contradict the existing trademark licence or liaison provisions.
